summary: Israeli-born entrepreneur Adam Neumann built the office-leasing firm WeWork into a venture-funded giant valued at 47 billion dollars on hype, self-dealing and a cult-like work culture, until its failed 2019 IPO forced him out with a huge payout.

evidence.note: Neumann's birth in Tel Aviv in 1979 and early childhood moves
family returns to Israel in 1990; long segment on kibbutz life shaping his ideas
Green Desk co-working venture founded in Dumbo around the 2008 crash
Neumann buys buildings and leases them back to WeWork, self-dealing
cleaners' union protest over low-paid non-union labor
extended comparison of WeWork culture to a cult, including NXIVM parallels
2017 summer camp moved to the English countryside
Rebekah Neumann's WeGrow private school and its problems
2019 IPO filing, Wall Street Journal expose and Neumann's ouster

notes: Neumann is alive; lifetime rule gives covered_span 1979-2019 (release year). main_span ends at the 2019 ouster. WeWork kept secondary since the story is built around Neumann. Primary theme is a judgment call between finance-crypto (VC/real-estate bubble) and fraud-grift. cults-new-religions used for the long cult-like culture segment though WeWork is not a religion. Heavy drinking culture discussed but not tagged drug-use. Guest surnames from my knowledge of Knowledge Fight hosts.
